Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The New Zealand players stride out to the middle, followed by Liton Das and Mohammad Naim. Hamish Bennett will start with the ball.
... Run Chase ...

Right then! 94 to win for Bangladesh to seal the series. It seems easy but they were bowled out for under 100 in the last game, so you cannot count New Zealand out of this game. The chase promises to be an exciting one. Do join us for that in a short while.

New Zealand never got used to the pace of the pitch. They started poorly losing Rachin Ravindra in the first over. Finn Allen threatened for a while but he fell to a poor shot. There was a partnership between Latham and Young but the former did not last long. Young was the only one to get going as he scored a fine 46. There was nothing much from the others and New Zealand were bowled out for just 93.

For Bangladesh, it was all about Nasum Ahmed! He was simply sensational as he picked up 4 wickets and gave away just 10 runs in his 4 overs. Mustafizur Rahman was terrific as well, especially at the death. The other spinners too were good with the ball. The thing that will please Bangladesh the most would be their fielding. They were very good and took some excellent catches in the field.

Another excellent bowling performance from Bangladesh! They have done really well to restrict New Zealand to a low score and now have a good chance to win the series with one game to spare. New Zealand will be disappointed with their batting effort as apart from Will Young, no one showed the desire to fight it out in the middle.

OUT! That's it! Mustafizur adds one more to his tally. Delivers it full and outside off, another cutter, Blair Tickner clears his front leg to possibly drive it over covers but only manages to slice it straight into the hands of Mahedi Hasan at short third man. New Zealand are bowled out for 93.
Commentary.Howout: c Mahedi Hasan b Mustafizur Rahman

Commentary.Commentary: Hamish Bennett is the last man in.

OUT! Will Young departs. Rahman comes up with yet another slower one, short and around off, angling away, Young steps back to pump it over covers but fails to get the timing right. Mahmudullah runs back a bit and takes the catch safely. Young is gone after playing a handy knock.
Slower one, on a length around leg, Tickner is early into the shot and flicks it aerially towards square leg. The fielder attacks it across to his right but the ball drops safely. They take a single.

Aims for a yorker but it turns out to be a full toss, Blair pushes it to covers and they cross for a brisk run. Mohammad Saifuddin has a shy at the striker's end but misses. A bit strange from Will Young to pick a run off the last ball.
Blair Tickner is the next man in.

OUT! The middle stump is obliterated. A cracking yorker, right in the blockhole, Ajaz Patel is late in bringing his bat down and it sneaks past him to uproot the middle stump. Mohammad Saifuddin has his first wicket of the match and would love to pick another one off his final ball.

Shortish and on off, angling away, Ajaz steps back and slaps it through the line. Finds Mahmudullah at covers and Patel is annoyed with himself. Either side of that fielder and it would have been a boundary.
Fuller and on off, this one is drilled to deep cover for a single.
Clever change in pace. Slower in pace, short in length, around off, Will Young jumps across the stumps for the paddle shot but fails to connect. Beaten in line, length and pace.
Right in the blockhole, Ajaz digs it out and the ball takes his pads before rolling near the popping crease. Young calls his partner through for a quick run.
Mohammad Saifuddin will bowl the 19th over.

Slower one, short and outside off, Young punches it from the back foot but fails to beat the diving cover fielder. Mahmudullah there saves at least two runs. 12 legal balls left in the innings, how many more can New Zealand add to their 89?
FOUR! That's an absolute beauty! Fuller in length around leg, slower in pace, Will Young steps back, runs down the track and smashes it over the bowler's head. A boundary results at long on.
Shortish and on middle, Ajaz turns it down to fine leg and hands the strike back to Young.
Fuller and straighter on middle, Young helps it in front of square leg for a run as the bowler himself runs after it to stop the ball.
Back of a length, around leg and angling down, Ajaz is surprised by the lack of bounce and fails to work it away. The ball pings him on the thigh pad, rests near the pitch and they pinch a leg bye.
Fullish and around off, slower in pace and cutting back in, Patel flicks it aerially but it doesn't carry to the fielder at square leg.
Tossed up outside off, Young looks to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Loopy ball on middle, Young dances down the track and then lifts it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
On off, pushed to point for one.
Tossed up on the pads, Young looks to flick but it goes off the pads to the off side. A leg bye taken.
Tossed up on middle, Patel sweeps it to deep square leg for one.
Floated on the pads, Young works it to the leg side for one.
Ajaz Patel is the new batsman. Also, Shakib Al Hasan is back on to bowl his last over.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! What a catch off his own bowling! This is a terrific catch and New Zealand slip further. Slower ball on off, McConchie is deceived by the slowness of the delivery. He is early into the shot and hence checks it at the final moment. But ends up chipping it to the left of Mustafizur. He dives and plucks it out of thin air with his left hand. Sensational.
Slower ball once again, it's outside off, Young looks to pull but is early into the shot and he misses.
Slower ball on off, McConchie pushes it with an angled bat to point.
WIDE! Down the leg side, McConchie lets it go. Wided.
Full on the pads, Young flicks it to mid-wicket for a single.
Cole McConchie is the new batsman.

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellent catch from Mohammad Naim and Blundell goes! Mustafizur takes the pace off the ball and bowls it on middle, Blundell looks to go over mid on but does not get enough power behind it. The ball loops in the air, Naim runs across to his left from mid on and dives to take a brilliant catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Naim b Mustafizur Rahman

Commentary.Commentary: Full on the pads, Blundell looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. Mustafizur Rahman appeals but then gestures that it's going down.
Mustafizur Rahman is back into the attack. Gave just 3 runs in his first over.
Shortish and on off, Will moves inside the crease and works it on the leg side. Finds mid-wicket. 7 from the over, New Zealand are 72/5 with 30 balls left in the innings. Can they get to 120?
Full and outside off, Young goes down to sweep but misses. It brushes his boot and loops behind. A stifled appeal for an lbw but the impact is well outside off.

SIX! Fine shot! Mahmudullah flights this one around off, full and spinning in, Young goes down on one knee and hammers it over mid-wicket for a biggie. He is New Zealand's big hope at the moment. Moves to 34.
This one stays low! Full and around off, spinning in, Young does well to keep his eyes on the ball and defends it near his front pad.
Flatter off spinner, on the shorter side, Young goes back and punches it to covers.
Starts with a short ball around leg, Blundell gets back and hits it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tom Blundell is getting some treatment done from the New Zealand physio on his leg. He seems to be suffering from cramps. Mahmudullah is into the attack.

Dropped? Fuller and on middle, Young advances down the track and drives it straight back. Saifuddin tries to stop it in his followthrough but it brushes his fingers and deflects behind. The long on fielder cuts it off and the batters take two. That appeared to be a bump ball. Mohammad Saifuddin has possibly hurt his fingers and the physio is taking him to the dressing room. Bleeding.
On middle, a length ball, Will wrists it across the line but finds mid-wicket.
Fullish and around off, Will steps back and drives but finds the cover fielder.
FOUR! That's nicely played! Good use of the feet. Will Young anticipates a slower one, it's around off, Young skips down the track and whips it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Slower one, full and around leg, Blundell works it off the inner half of his blade to fine leg for a single.
Full and angling in on middle, Young eases it through wide mid on for a single.
Slow spin, from around off, Blundell gets back and helps it to mid-wicket. Young wants a run but is sent back as the fielder inside the ring dives to stop the ball.
Flighted and full around off, Will plays yet another impressive sweep shot and sends it to deep square leg for a single.
Short and on middle, Blundell hops and punches it down to long on for a run.
Short and outside off, Young taps it down wide of short third man for a quick run.
Flighted delivery, on middle, some extra bounce, Tom Blundell gets back and somehow works it in the gap at backward square leg for a single.
Flatter and on middle, swept through square leg for a single.
A touch flatter and short on off, Tom defends it from the back foot.  A double-wicket maiden for Nasum Ahmed. Awesome. His figures read, 4-2-10-4!
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it back.
Almost edges it! Floated one, full and around off, spinning away, Blundell gets back, tries to push inside the line initially but then pulls his bat back.
Tom Blundell will face the Hat-Trick ball.

OUT! De Grandhomme has a golden duck! Nasum is on fire, on a hat-trick now. Tossed up delivery, full and around off, spinning away with some extra bounce, Colin de Grandhomme strides forward to defend but it takes the higher half of his bat and lobs behind. Nurul Hasan shows good reflexes as he catches it superbly.
Commentary.Howout: c Nurul Hasan b Nasum Ahmed

Commentary.Commentary: Who comes out now? Colin de Grandhomme it is.

OUT! SOUND OF TIMBER! Henry Nicholls plays across the line to a nicely pitched up delivery and pays the price. Loopy and full around off, Nicholls presses forward but plays all over it. The ball lands, spins back in sharply and shatters the stumps behind. New Zealand are in a spot of bother. Nasum Ahmed is jumping in celebration after picking his third wicket of the match.
Shortish arm ball around off, Nicholls stays back and plays it down to short third man.
Tossed it up around leg, full in length, Nicholls knocks it down through mid on and opens his account with a single.
A touch flatter and full on middle, Henry flicks but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Floated one, full and around off, Nicholls gets forward and defends it to the off side.
Henry Nicholls is the next man in.

OUT! Latham is stumped and the blossoming partnership has been nipped in the bud. Lovely delivery, enticing the batsman with his flight, Latham runs down the track to work a full ball around but it lands and spins past his blade. Nurul Hasan does the rest and Tom doesn't even bother to look behind. New Zealand will have to rebuild again.
Commentary.Howout: st Nurul Hasan b Mahedi Hasan

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and shorter around off, turning in, Young goes back and punches it through mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Will Young has been quite effective with his sweep shot. Full and around leg, Will goes down and sweeps it sweetly to the long leg fence. 50 up!
Bowling change. Mahedi Hasan is back on.
Loopy ball on the pads, Young clips it to mid-wicket for a single as the bowler himself runs after the ball. New Zealand are 46/2 at the halfway mark.
Tossed up on off, Latham defends it to covers and takes a quick run.
Short on the pads, pulled to deep square leg for a single.
Flatter on off, Young defends it back to the bowler off the outer half of his blade.
Mid on comes up.
Short ball on off, Latham pulls it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Flatter ball on off, Latham guides it to short third man.
Loopy ball on middle, Latham uses his feet and flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Flatter on middle, Young nudges it to mid on for a single.
Tossed up on middle, Young dances down the track and defends it to mid-wicket at the last moment.
FOUR! That's well played by Young! Flighted ball on off, Young gets down and across the stumps and then sweeps it to deep backward square leg for a boundary.
Floated outside off, Young goes on his knees and attempts the reverse lap sweep but fails to put any bat on it.
Tossed up on off, Latham looks to sweep but it takes the inside edge, hits the pads and goes to square leg. A single taken.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on. Change of ends for him. 0/11 in his 2 overs so far.
Fullish ball on middle, Latham shuffles across and flicks it to the leg side to end the over with another single.
Good length around middle, Young works it to deep square leg for another single.
Short ball on off, Latham moves across and pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Full on off, Young defends it to covers for a single.
Slower ball outside off, Young looks to push inside the line but misses.
Full outside off, Latham drives it to deep cover for a single.
Mohammad Saifuddin is inserted into the attack.
Flighted ball outside off, Latham pushes it to covers for one.
On middle, defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! Nicely played! Full on the pads, Latham tickles it towards fine leg. Mustafizur Rahman tries hard to stop it at short fine leg but it goes past him and into the fine leg fence.
Flatter ball on the pads, Latham clips it to the deep square leg region for a couple.

Time for the Decision Review System. Mahmudullah has once again listened to the advice of Nurul Hasan, the keeper, and taken the review. It's for an lbw against Tom Latham. Is the impact outside off? Forget that, there is some glove involved. Bangladesh have now wasted both their reviews.

NOT OUT! It has hit the gloves! Tossed up around off, Latham looks to play the reverse sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal is made for LBW but the umpire is not interested. The Bangladesh skipper, Mahmudullah takes the review. The UltraEdge shows a spike as the ball passed the gloves. Bangladesh waste another review and are now left with none.
Tossed up on off, swept to deep square leg for a single.
Good length and on the pads, Young nudges it to square leg for one. New Zealand are 22 for 2 at the end of the Powerplay.
Another slower ball on off, Young looks to defend but it takes the outside edge and lobs to point where it falls short of the fielder.
Slower ball on off, Young uses his feet and then pushes it to covers.
Full ball on off, Latham defends it to point and takes a quick single.
Good length around the pads, Young tucks it to the leg side for one at backward square leg.
Full ball on middle and leg, Young dances down the track and looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge to point.
Mustafizur Rahman is into the attack now.
Quicker around off, Latham is forward as he defends it to the off side. A good start from Mahedi.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Loopy and around off, it's swept over square leg for a single.
Beaten all ends up! Fuller and around off, dipping in and going straight on, Young tries to go big initially but then attempts to defend. The ball though skids off the surface and beats the edge.
Loopy and full around off, Latham drives it down to long off for a single.
Quicker arm ball on off, Latham defends it to mid-wcket.
Mahedi Hasan is into the attack.
Ufff...unplayable! Yet another arm ball around off, this has some extra bounce too, Young tries to defend but it beats the edge.
Arm ball around off, Young does well to defend it from the back foot.
Fires it in, full and on off, Latham tries to flick but gets a leading edge. It goes safely to extra cover and they cross.
Spinning away again, full and outside off, Tom is beaten on the drive this time.
Turning away from the batsman, Latham tries to sweep but misses.
Quicker and flatter on off, kept out to mid-wicket.
Review time! Bangladesh have taken a review for LBW! They think that it is pad first but the replays show that it has hit only the bat and not the pad. Poor, poor review.

NOT OUT! Superb follow-up delivery by Nasum Ahmed. After getting the last ball to turn away sharply with extra bounce, this one shoots low as it skids into the batsman from a fuller length around off. Will Young has his bat down just in time to keep it out. The bowler appeals thinking it's pad first but it's turned down. Mahmudullah is advised by the keeper to take the DRS but the replays show that the ball had found the middle of the bat. A review wasted. Very poor from Nurul.
Beauty! Turn. Bounce. Wow. Floated one, landing around off and spinning square, Young stands back, completely clueless and it turns past his defensive blade.
Will Young makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! Live by the sword, die by the sword. Finn Allen is gone. You can call his shot selection silly now as he failed to execute it properly. Nasum delivers it flat and full around off, Allen again attempts for his reverse-batted heave but this time mistimes it badly. He ends up playing it aerially to backward point and Mohammad Saifuddin has another catch in the match.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Saifuddin b Nasum Ahmed

Commentary.Commentary: Nasum drags his length short, around off, Latham goes back and plays it down to covers for a quick run.
Flatter and shorter, wide outside off, Allen goes back and slaps to deep cover. The fielder in the deep does well to stop it from crossing the rope and saves one run.
Another reverse-batted shot from Allen, not timed too well but it clears the infield on the off side. It goes to sweeper cover and they take a couple.
Drags his length short and delivers it on middle, Finn pulls it to deep square leg for a single.

SIX! What a shot! Out of nowhere. Before this delivery, Nurul Hasan, the keeper, was saying - not easy to play big shots here. This shot in a way proves him wrong. Floated one, full and around off, Finn Allen brings out the reverse-batted shot and heaves it over covers for a biggie.
Quicker one, flat and on middle, Finn goes back and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Aerial but safe! Arm ball on middle, skidding in, Allen gets back to flick but closes the face of the bat early. It takes the leading edge but falls safely at covers.
Floated and on middle, Tom goes back and turns it towards square leg for one.
New Zealand are away! Short in length and outside off, Latham goes back and cuts it through cover-point for a couple of runs.
Who will bowl from the other end? Shakib Al Hasan it is.
Flatter and shorter outside off, some extra bounce, Allen goes back and does well to defend it down safely. End of a successful first over by Nasum Ahmed, a wicket maiden.
Tom Latham is the next man in.

OUT! Fantastic catch from Mohammad Saifuddin. First strike for Bangladesh. There was no need for that shot. Slower through the air, full and landing around off, spinning in a bit, Ravindra goes down on one knee for the slog-sweep but it takes the top edge of his bat. It flies behind backward square leg. Two fielders are interested but Mohammad Saifuddin calls for it coming from short fine leg and completes the catch with a full-length dive. He had another fielder in his peripheral vision and did well to call for it to avoid the collision.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Saifuddin b Nasum Ahmed

Commentary.Commentary: Gets back inside the crease and works it with the spin on the leg side. Finds mid-wicket.
Leans forward to a full ball around off and defends it to the off side. The bowler moves across to his right to collect the ball.
This one holds its line. Flatter one, short and outside off, Ravindra allows it through to the keeper.
Big turn! Tossed up ball on middle, gripping and spinning into the left-hander, Ravindra goes back and keeps it out to mid-wicket.
We are all set to begin! The Bangladesh players stride out to the middle, followed by Finn Allen and Rachin Ravindra. Nasum Ahmed has the ball in hand and he will bowl the first over. Here we go...

Mahmudullah, the captain of Bangladesh, says that winning the series against Australia was a big boost but this is a new series against a different team and hopes to seal the series today. Tells us that it was not complacency in the last match, it's just that they didn't capitalize on the start with the bat. Adds that they have played very well in the recent past and the last loss won't change anything. Informs that Bangladesh are unchanged.

Tom Latham, the New Zealand skipper, says that the bowlers have been fantastic throughout and they have adapted to international cricket very well. Adds that to put a competitive score on the board is the plan and they need to put partnerships. Informs that they have got two changes as Blair Tickner comes in for Jacob Duffy and Hamish Bennett comes in for Scott Kuggeleijn.

Pitch report - Atul Wassan says that this is the same pitch where the second game was played. Adds that there is grass on it but it is dead grass. Tells that there is no moisture on it and it looks like a better batting pitch. Says that the average score in the last 10 games is around 117 which is very low. Opines that the team winning the toss should look to bat first.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Rachin Ravindra, Will Young, Tom Latham (WK/C), Colin de Grandhomme, Henry Nicholls, Tom Blundell, Cole McConchie, Ajaz Patel, Blair Tickner (IN PLACE OF JACOB DUFFY), Hamish Bennett (IN PLACE OF SCOTT KUGGELEIJN).

Bangladesh (Unchanged Playing XI) - Mohammad Naim, Liton Das, Shakib Al Hasan, Mushfiqur Rahim, Mahmudullah (C), Afif Hossain, Nurul Hasan (WK), Mahedi Hasan, Mohammad Saifuddin, Mustafizur Rahman, Nasum Ahmed.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of New Zealand. They have elected to bat first.

Bangladesh got a bit of a reality check in the last match as they lost by a big margin in conditions that suited them more. It was their batting not doing well that day and the Bangla Tigers would look to improve in that area. They would be the favourites once again but New Zealand have shown that they are no pushovers in these conditions despite being short on experience and resources. Should be a close game. Stay tuned for more...

Two teams are in Asia currently playing international cricket - New Zealand and South Africa. Both have been put to the sword by the spinners but have fared decently. Last evening, South Africa fought superbly with the ball but their batting let them down as they lost the series. New Zealand are in a similar situation and would want to avoid a lacklustre batting show with the series on the line. Another trial by spin awaits them.

Warm welcome, folks! It's 2-1 in favour of Bangladesh but the last win of New Zealand has certainly spiced up this 5-match T20I series. Australia had also managed to win one match recently in Bangladesh but that came when the series was already done and dusted. The Black Caps here have given themselves a good chance to draw level and push this series into the decider. Can they do it? Let's find out.
... Game Day ...
